title: Changes in Sensitivity, Taste and Smell in Stroke Patients
official: Changes in Sensitivity of Swallowing-relevant Structures, Taste and Smell in Stroke Patients
summary: This study evaluates changes in swallowing using endoscopic swallowing studies and measuring of pharyngeal sensitivity, taste and smell in stroke patients. Younger (\<60 years) and older (\>60 years) volunteers will serve as control.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Volunteers:

* informed consent

Stroke patients:

* informed consent
* new supratentorial stroke (\<72 hours old) confirmed by CT (computed tomography) or MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)

Exclusion Criteria:

* pre-existing stroke oder dysphagia
* extensive white matter lesions in CT- or MRI-scan
* allergies to odorous substances or flavoring
* contraindications for FEES (flexible endoscopic evaluation of swallowing), CT or MRI (stroke patients only)
